plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Brisbane's streets and parks turn violet-blue as jacaranda canopies fill with clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers. When the petals fall, they leave a soft purple carpet on the pavement below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to November, with peak bloom in October and early November
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, not Australia. It has been planted so widely in Brisbane that its bloom is now a signature sight of the Queensland spring.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens delicate, often lightly scented, single to peony-like blossoms while most gardens are winding down for autumn. Its petals fade into pink and white drifts under the dark foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn to early winter, with its main flush in early November
plants.location: Cool-temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere, such as Cornwall in southwest England, and its native southern Japan
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are among the first camellias to flower each year. The leaves of a close relative, Camellia sinensis, are used to make tea.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: In autumn gardens across Japan, chrysanthemums open in layered, spidery or ball-shaped blooms. They are shown at flower festivals and in parks such as Tokyo's Shinjuku Gyoen.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to mid-November in Japan, often through November and December as potted and cultivated forms
plants.location: Japan, especially Tokyo and other temperate regions
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum is Japan's national flower and a symbol of the Imperial Family. It blooms because lengthening nights trigger flowering, not warmth.
